subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• On September 25, 1513, Vasco Núñez de Balboa became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas.
• On November 8, 1519, Hernán Cortés arrived in Tenochtitlan, the capital of the Aztec Empire.
• Cortés's arrival marked the beginning of Spanish conquest in central Mexico.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the order in which Balboa and Cortés made their historic discoveries. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Balboa, who sighted the Pacific Ocean in 1513, made his discovery several years before Cortés reached Tenochtitlan in 1519.
choices.B: On November 8, 1519, Cortés's arrival marked the beginning of Spanish conquest in central Mexico.
choices.C: Two Spanish explorers made significant discoveries in the Americas during the early 16th century.
choices.D: The same decade that Cortés reached Tenochtitlan—the 1510s—Spanish conquest began in central Mexico.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes the order in which Balboa and Cortés made their discoveries, noting that Balboa sighted the Pacific several years before Cortés reached Tenochtitlan.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. While the sentence indicates that two explorers made discoveries in the same time period, it doesn't identify which explorer made which discovery when; as a result, it doesn't emphasize the order in which Balboa and Cortés made their discoveries.
